label: Rock shore
summary: Grass and moss in the cracks of the rock slabs by a big lake, heath on their ledges and thin soil, scrub hugging the rock and along the water, and grass under and between the bushes.
steps: Reads Unity's surface map of the built course (golfmap.surfaces.export) and the course DEM next to it, both at 0.5 m cells: the rock slabs (surface Slab) and the water come from the map, the slope from the DEM.
Finds the big lake: the largest connected water body of the map, if it is at least lake-min. A pond or a creek pool is not a shore.
Plants only on the shore: within lake-reach of the lake and on a slab or within slab-reach of one, both fading over reach-ramp. With inland above 0 every slab is dressed, lake or not.

Crack (rock_shore/crack, a mix layer): grass and moss in noise patches on the rock, favouring ledges (gentle slope) and never on faces steeper than face-slope, plus a ragged fringe in over the slab's edge and a skirt out onto the land beside it.
Heath (rock_shore/heath): heather and lingonberry in sparse patches on the slab's ledges and on the thin soil just outside it.

Scrub (rock_shore/scrub): bushes on land in a band out from the slab's edge, densest against the rock and thinning inland, and along the lake's water; in clumps that close up against the rock. Inland slabs get a narrower band at the inland weight.
Grass (rock_shore/grass, a mix layer): grass under the bushes and between the clumps in the same band.

Keeps clear of tees, greens, fairways, semi, bunkers and blend strips with the tall rough's clearances (tall-grass clearances, without water and rock: a shore bush stands on the waterline and against the rock), of houses (the tall rough's building margin, fading in over block-ramp), and of the paths and roads, cut out of the polygons as the tall rough cuts them.

Which plants each variant holds is the course's grass palette and bindings; the variant keys crack, heath, scrub and grass are fixed. Scrub and heath replace the tall rough and woodland floor beneath them; grass and crack plant over whatever is there.
Each variant's weight field is written as nested contour bands, one zone per band polygon, stacked scrub, heath, grass, crack from the bottom.

rules.text: The largest water body of the map is the big lake only if it is at least this large.
The shore: within this of the big lake ...
... and on a rock slab or within this of one.
Both limits fade over this, centred on them.
0 = the shore only; above 0 every slab gets crack and heath in full, and scrub and grass away from the lake at this weight.
Away from the lake (inland above 0) the scrub band ends this far from the slab's edge.
The land scrub, grass, heath and the crack skirt grow on (never on the slab).
Nothing on land within this of the lake: no bush with its foot in the water.
The DEM is smoothed over this before the slope is taken (lidar speckle).
A ledge: full below the first slope, none above the second.
Rock steeper than this is a face: nothing grows on it.
Share of the slab (not faces) under crack patches.
Size of the crack patches' noise blobs.
How much a ledge counts against the noise: the patches favour ledges.
The patch edge fades over this much noise either side of the cut-off (heath patches too).
Reaches in over the slab's edge (0 to 2 x this by noise) ...
... and out onto the land beside it (0 to 2 x this by noise).
Size of the noise blobs that make the fringe and skirt ragged.
Share of the ledges and thin soil under heath patches.
Thin soil: this far out from the slab's edge.
On the thin soil the heath fades out over the last metres of heath-reach.
On the slab heath grows only where the ledge weight is above this.
Size of the heath patches' noise blobs.
The scrub band begins this far off the slab's edge (the crack fringe and skirt are there) ...
... is full from the first to the second distance ...
... and thins to scrub-far-weight at this distance from the slab's edge.
The band's density at its outer edge.
Beyond the band (and the inland band) it is gone over this.
Scrub also grows along the lake within this of its water ...
... full to this, then thinning to nothing at shore-band ...
... at this density.
Size of the scrub clumps' noise blobs.
Noise from the first to the second value takes a clump from none to full (about two thirds of the band).
Against the rock the clumps close up: the noise is lifted by this at the slab's edge ...
... fading out from the first to the second distance from it.
The grass between the clumps, as a share of the band's weight (under a clump, the clump's).
The tall rough's clearances are kept, except from these (a shore bush stands on the waterline and against the rock).
Beyond the house margin (the tall rough's building-margin) it fades in over this.
The zone type of the zones.
These variants plant over what grows there (blend mix); the others replace it.
The contour levels each weight field is written at (one zone per band; the top band has weight 1).
Feather of each band zone.
Edge noise of the band zones (none: the fields' own edges are ragged).
Outlines are simplified to this tolerance.
Band pieces smaller than this are dropped, per variant.
